paper.title: Two-Fidelity Best-Action Identification for Stochastic Minimax Tree

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-confidence best-action identification in two-fidelity stochastic minimax trees
unmapped: Finite balanced minimax tree of depth D with alternating Max/Min nodes; goal is to identify the optimal root action (minimax value)

Two-fidelity oracles at any exposed non-root node: a cheap deterministic fast oracle with bias bounded by a known envelope B(h(v)) depending on remaining depth, and an expensive (cost c>=1) unbiased sigma-sub-Gaussian slow oracle
The learner knows the fast-oracle bias envelope B and the slow-oracle cost c
Performance measured by total query cost C_tau = N^F + c * sum_v N_v^S rather than number of samples
Nodes must be expanded (exposed) before they can be queried
settings.definition_quote: We study fixed-confidence best-action identification (BAI) in stochastic minimax trees... The fast oracle (m=1) is cheap and deterministic, but may be biased. The slow oracle (m=2) is more expensive and stochastic, but unbiased for the true minimax value V^*(v)... repeated slow-oracle queries return independent \sigma-sub-Gaussian samples Y_{v,s} with distribution \nu_{v,2} and mean \mu_{v,2}=V^*(v).

settings.name_in_paper: Two-fidelity minimax tree BAI with biased slow oracle (MARL application)
unmapped: Finite balanced minimax tree with two-fidelity oracles (fast deterministic biased within envelope B, slow stochastic)
Slow oracle has fixed mean V^*(v)+b_v with bias |b_v| <= xi; the learner knows the bias bound xi
Slow samples satisfy a time-uniform concentration (Eq. conf-radius) around the biased mean
The learner knows the fast-oracle envelope B
settings.definition_quote: Suppose the slow oracle has fixed mean $V^*(v)+b_v$, with known $\xi\ge\max_v|b_v|$, and its samples satisfy Eq.~\eqref{eq:conf-radius} around this mean.

conditions: feasible confidence allocation sum_v delta_v <= delta
tuning: confidence radius beta_v time-uniform at level delta_v

source.label: thm:pac-correct
source.quote: Fix any feasible confidence allocation \(\boldsymbol{\delta}=(\delta_v)\) and any \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). Consider Algorithm~\ref{alg:2ffs-t} run with accuracy \(\varepsilon\), let \(\tau\) be its stopping time... Then, \( \mathbb P( \tau<\infty \text{ and } V^*(r,a^*)-V^*(r,\hat a_\tau)>\varepsilon ) \le \delta \).

results.notes: (epsilon,delta)-PAC correctness; finite stopping not guaranteed by this theorem. Objective mapping (bai_fixed_confidence with epsilon) approximate.

symbols.P_D: depth-overhead factor defined by recursion P_h = max{(1+alpha_h)Lambda_loc, (1+Lambda_pre/alpha_h)P_{h-1}}, P_0=Lambda_loc
symbols.H_delta: recursive oracle complexity H(delta) = |Ch(r)| + sum_a J_a^*(delta) for the confidence allocation

conditions: Assumption 3.3 (local dyadic scale regularity with constants Lambda_pre, Lambda_gap)
holds on event E_delta of probability >= 1-delta

source.label: thm:budgeted-general-depth
source.quote: Fix any feasible confidence allocation ... satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:local-scale-regularity}, and run Algorithm~\ref{alg:2ffs-t} with \(\varepsilon=0\). On \(\mathcal E_\delta\), the algorithm is guaranteed to stop at a finite time \(\tau\), returns \(\hat a_\tau=a^*\), and satisfies \( C_\tau \le P_D\,H(\boldsymbol{\delta}) \).

results.notes: Bound is on total query cost C_tau (fast queries + c times slow queries), recorded as sample_complexity. Also gives finite stopping and exact identification on E_delta.

symbols.H_star: optimized recursive oracle complexity, infimum over feasible allocations of H(delta)

conditions: regularity constants Lambda_pre, Lambda_gap uniform along a near-optimal feasible allocation sequence (Assumption 3.3)
constants hidden depend on Lambda_pre, Lambda_gap
tuning: allocation delta^eta with H(delta^eta) <= H^* + eta, eta <= H^*

source.label: thm:budgeted-general-depth
source.quote: In particular, when \(\alpha_h=(h+1)^2\) and the local regularity constants are uniform constants, \[ C_\tau \le \mathcal{O}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{pre}},\Lambda_{\mathrm{gap}}} (D^2(H^*+\eta)), \] and, since \(H^*\ge |\mathrm{Ch}(r)|\ge 2\), one obtains \(\mathcal{O}(D^2H^*)\) by taking \(\eta\le H^*\)

results.notes: Cost bound in terms of H^*; the exact intermediate form C_tau <= P_D(H^*+eta) w.p. >= 1-delta also stated. H^* is an analysis-only reference complexity, not a lower bound.

conditions: slow oracle mean V^*(v)+b_v with known xi >= max_v |b_v|
samples satisfy time-uniform concentration around biased mean
tuning: slow radius beta_v replaced by beta_v + xi

source.label: thm:biased-slow
source.quote: Suppose the slow oracle has fixed mean $V^*(v)+b_v$, with known $\xi\ge\max_v|b_v|$, and its samples satisfy Eq.~\eqref{eq:conf-radius} around this mean. Replacing each slow radius $\beta_v$ by $\beta_v+\xi$ preserves the $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ finite-output correctness of 2FFS. The bias inflation does not accumulate with tree depth.

results.notes: Only correctness of finite outputs; finite stopping and cost bounds do not carry over.

conditions: proxy envelope hat B nondecreasing with hat B(0)=0 and hat B(h) >= B(h) for all h
tuning: fast-oracle envelope B replaced by proxy hat B

source.label: thm:loose-envelope
source.quote: Let \(B(h)\) denote the true fast-oracle envelope, and let \(\hat B(h)\) be a nondecreasing proxy envelope with $\hat B(0)=0$ and $\hat B(h)\ge B(h)$ for all \(h\). Replacing \(B(h)\) with \(\hat B(h)\) preserves the finite-output PAC guarantee and, on $\mathcal E_\delta$ for the same query history, can only widen the resulting confidence intervals.

results.notes: Learner knows a conservative proxy envelope rather than the true B.
